description:
Why do things fall down, and never up? Gizmo the robot watches an apple drop from a tree, races a heavy ball against a light ball, lets a feather float down and looks out into space at the Moon. A gentle science lesson for ages 4-8 with questions to answer, things to try and a quiz at the end.
Kids learn that gravity is an invisible pull, that the Earth pulls things toward its center so things fall and we stay on the ground, that a heavy ball and a light ball dropped together land together, that the air slows a feather down, that everything with mass has gravity, and that gravity keeps the Moon going around the Earth and the planets going around the Sun.

Gizmo Explains makes gentle, colorful videos for little learners. New videos every day! Made with care for ages 4-8. Every fact is checked against trusted sources and every script is reviewed for kid safety before publishing.

WHERE THE FACTS COME FROM
NASA Space Place (What is gravity?), University of Illinois Physics Van (Heavy and Light - Both Fall the Same), American Physical Society PhysicsQuest (Falling Physics).

title: Which Lands First? Gizmo Explains
description:
A heavy ball and a light ball: which lands first? Gizmo the robot drops them together, then races a ball against a feather. Heavy and light land at the same time; the air slows the feather down, and with no air a feather and a rock land together.
